Sweet Venom

Rina Kent

3.98

From the New York Times bestselling author Rina Kent comes a new standalone dark hockey romance set in a new glamorous secret world.

CAN I OUTRUN HIS MERCILESS OBSESSION?

I accidentally witnessed a brutal murder.
I froze, pretended I saw nothing, hoping I could leave it behind.
But my plan backfired, and my life spiraled downward.
Now I'm the target of cold-blooded revenge.

Jude Callahan isn't just a hockey god—he's a devil no one dares to cross.
My existence disrupts his stardom, prestige, and possible serial-killer career choice.
And he's set out to make me pay for that moment of silence.
No matter how much I run or hide, he finds me, watching from the shadows.

Like a predator.
I thought he'd stop at the stalking.
Or even better, he'd kill me and finally end my misery.
But Jude has other plans.
He say's I can't die. I have to pay for my sins.
And just like that, he drags me into his depraved world, kicking and screaming.

This book is part of the Vipers' series but can be read on its own.

About the author

Rina Kent

65 books75.5k followers
Rina Kent is a New York Times, USA Today, and #1 bestselling author of all things dark romance.
Better known for writing unapologetic anti-heroes and villains, Rina weaves tales of characters you shouldn’t fall for but inevitably do. Her stories are laced with a touch of darkness, a splash of angst, and just the right amount of unhealthy intensity.
When she’s not busy plotting mayhem for her ever-expanding Rinaverse, she leads a private life in London, travels, and pampers her cats in true Cat Lady fashion.

wow…i actually enjoyed this? when i first started reading, beautiful venom, i knew that that was not gonna be a favorite mine. rina kent’s books over the last couple years have been extremely hit or miss due to the excessive repetition with the plot and the characters. this book—while it’s very similar to every other book in her collection—had a lot of elements that made it more entertaining. i knew that this was a book that i was going to enjoy as soon as i was introduced to these characters in beautiful venom. i did a dual read with the audio and the physical and let me just say…teddy hamilton never fails me.

starting with the obvious here, the character dynamic and the overall plot is very similar to her previous works, so please be aware of that before you start reading. i’m not sure who described this as being similar to god of wrath, but i would argue it’s better. jude is what jeremy THOUGHT he was. this story is a stereotypical boy falls first, who is obsessed with her. unlike her recent works, jude was actually an MMC that i liked and was intrigued by. there are elements of this book that were extremely corny and you can tell that they were written by someone who is a lot older, which is typical in her books lol. otherwise, i’m actually shocked that i had fun reading this. sometimes we just need a brainless plot to fill the void.

as for the romance, i thought it was cute…god bless everyone since miss girl ain’t a virgin. we won. violet is a heroin who is actually able to stand alone and isn’t completely fueled by a man and his obsession with her. her plot and her story are completely separate from jude, which made this a little bit more interesting than her usual books. as for the actual romance plot here, there isn’t a whole lot of action that happens outside of them since jude is extremely committed to violet the second he sees her. she also barely pays attention to anybody since she has her own struggles from her childhood, which is now bleeding into her adult life. she does have the survival instincts of a shoe, making the drama and the tension lackluster. however, given their story, that is an element that i enjoyed since this type of book doesn’t need unnecessary theatrical soap-opera melodrama.

in typical rina style, there is a random mystery plot that is prevalent throughout the entire story which does nothing but fuel weird third act drama. i don’t even remember what was going on with that mystery plot, but to be honest, it wasn’t very relevant to the bigger picture. one of the highlights of this book is definitely preston. preston is a character that is a lot more pertinent given the friendship circle, and the set up for the next book. marcus and preston remind me a lot of jeremy and landon. that was one of the relationship’s that i did want to see flourish on paper, but unfortunately, rina had other ideas. i’m hoping that we see that similar dynamic in the next book because there are so much potential for that to be a good love story. aside from that—this is a feel good easy fun time so don’t expect peak literature, but i was here for a fun time, not a long time.

thank you to my best-friend, vee. i cant wait to read everything with you!

This is the best RK book of 2025 in my honest opinion.

I was cautiously excited for this one because of the crumbs that we got, but I was also a little scared because I didn't love Kiss the Villain or Beautiful Venom. No lie, I spent the entire book just praying for no borderline rape and non-con scenes like in KTV and BV. Thankfully, the scenes we got were consensual and actually kind of hot. Not dissing the other books, but there were certain scenes *cough* chapter six in bv *cough* that had me questioning what the fuck I read.

I have to also say that the pacing was off. And with that, compared to the first book, I didn't get much about the secret society in this one.

While I did somewhat enjoy this plot line and the book in general, I don't really understand the purpose of their whole stalker dynamic. Jude was mad at her because she was just watching while his mother gets stabbed. What, and I mean this in the most polite way ever, did he actually want her to do? He literally went around killing everyone that witnessed the "murder" and the whole thing turned out to be a suicide plot. And the thing is, there was no actual retribution for him about that and it was completely brushed under the rug.

It's so funny but Julian seems to be the sanest of everyone in these books. And he's basically a psychopath, going off what I've seen of him in these two books so far.

Violet has the self-preservation of a toddler, but at least she was self-aware about it. The relationship between Violet and Jude was nice and like I said above, I actually enjoyed it for the most part.

Dahlia saying that she had the hardest time when Violet was in a coma is comedic at best. This girl spent the entire time she was supposed to get revenge sucking Kane's dick in that book. Also, the way she consistently glazes up her (imo weird) boyfriend for absolutely no reason. She's so annoying that I was rolling my eyes every time she opened her mouth.

The Preston and Marcus crumbs are promising, so I'm going to remain cautiously excited for that one.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ — 4/5 ✨🪻🩵

“I'm broken too. We can fit our pieces together until we make something whole.”

This was one of those books that quietly found its way to me. It wasn’t an instant favorite from the first few chapters, but I never felt like giving up on it either. Instead, my interest grew little by little until I reached a point where I genuinely wanted to know how Violet and Jude’s story would unfold. 🥰

Since this is the second book in the series, I appreciated that it didn’t rely on repeating what had already been established. It trusted the reader to already know the world while giving these two characters the chance to leave their own mark.

By the time I turned the final pages, I realized this was one of those stories that simply needed patience before everything clicked into place. 😮‍💨

✦ beyond the obvious ✦

What I enjoyed most about this book was how comfortably it found its own place within the series. It expanded the world without losing sight of the characters, making the larger conflicts feel connected to the more personal ones.

The pacing gave important moments enough room to breathe, allowing decisions and consequences to carry real weight instead of being overshadowed by constant twists.

Rather than depending only on dramatic events, the story found its strength in watching its characters respond to everything happening around them, and that made the journey feel much more rewarding.

✦ the people behind the pages ✦

Violet Winters slowly became my favorite part of the story. I liked that she never felt one-dimensional. She knows how to stand her ground, yet the story never forgets to show the pain and emotions she carries beneath the surface.

Her decisions felt true to who she was instead of existing only to move the plot forward, which made it easier to understand her perspective even when I didn’t always agree with every choice she made.

What I appreciated most about Violet was that her growth came from learning to see herself differently. Watching her slowly let go of the pain she carried and start choosing herself made her journey feel genuinely rewarding. 🥹

Jude Callahan immediately stood out because he always seemed completely certain of himself, yet the story gradually showed that there was more driving his actions than simple arrogance. That balance made him much more interesting than my first impression suggested.

I appreciated that he had his own voice within the story instead of existing only as the romantic lead. His choices reflected who he was, and that gave his role a stronger purpose throughout the book.

Watching him alongside Violet made both characters more interesting because each of them brought out qualities in the other that might have remained hidden otherwise. 👀

✦ where everything came alive ✦

For me, Violet and Jude’s dynamic was the heart of the book. Their connection wasn’t built around grand declarations or instant understanding, but around two people whose differences constantly challenged the way they saw each other.

Some of my favorite moments came from their conversations and interactions because they revealed as much about their personalities as they did about their relationship.

Their chemistry felt earned, and I enjoyed watching their connection evolve through both the easier moments and the more complicated ones. 🤭

✦ after the final page ✦

Looking back, what stayed with me the most wasn’t a single scene or dramatic moment, but the journey these characters went through and the way they grew because of it.

Violet and Jude are the reason this book worked so well for me, and following their story made this installment feel genuinely worthwhile.

I’m glad I stayed with their story, and I’m looking forward to seeing where the series takes these characters next. 🫶🏻

My rating of The Vipers Series:

1. Beautiful Venom — 4.25 ⭐️
2. Sweet Venom — 4 ⭐️
3. Tempting Venom — TBR

Am I the only one who fully got Cecily and Jeremy?? I didn’t hate it but I swear I was getting déjà vu the whole time.
This is honestly pretty tame for Rina Kent and I can say that confidently as someone who’s basically read her entire catalog at this point. Don’t get me wrong, it’s still dark romance, but like… Rina-light.

They were cute, they gave me what I was kind of expecting, but I weirdly think they were WAY more interesting as side characters (that might just be a me thing idk). Like dahlia and Kane were so interesting again😭
We have mommy issues, daddy issues, everybody issues. A full buffet.

Plot wise it was good not her best but she definitely has worse so I’ll take it.

Their chemistry? I liked it. Cute. Fun.
But also… they just weren’t that memorable for me 😭

Now PRESTON???
The most interesting man in this whole book.

I can’t WAIT for his book 😝

Also I LOVED Violet and Dahlia’s relationship they were honestly adorable together. Violet babies her so much it was so cute.🥹💗

"𝘚𝘰𝘮𝘦 𝘯𝘦𝘦𝘥 𝘵𝘰 𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘨𝘦 𝘵𝘰 𝘧𝘪𝘯𝘥 𝘭𝘰𝘷𝘦.
𝘐 𝘫𝘶𝘴𝘵 𝘯𝘦𝘦𝘥𝘦𝘥 𝘵𝘰 𝘧𝘪𝘯𝘥 𝘮𝘺𝘴𝘦𝘭𝘧 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘩𝘦𝘭𝘱 𝘰𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘭𝘰𝘷𝘦 𝘰𝘧 𝘮𝘺 𝘭𝘪𝘧𝘦."





Okay, that definitely hit different. I genuinely enjoyed this book… a lot 😭💚. I loved Jude and Violet even before reading it, and now I love them even more together.

I don’t see violet as weak at all — she’s a girl who went through a lot of childhood trauma, and it pushed her to isolate herself and lose confidence. What I loved the most is how Jude played a big role in helping her change, stand up for herself, and start doing beautiful things for herself, because she finally began to see she deserved it. I adored the moment she slapped him and he laughed, saying how proud he was of her, or when he asked her who she dressed up for and she said “for myself,” and once again he told her he was proud 🥺 Even her suicidal thoughts faded, and she started wanting to live… He did so many good things for her, always supporting her in every moment.

But let’s not forget he did terrify her at some point (and I’m not talking about the stalking — something else entirely). If that hadn’t happened, Jude Callahan would’ve been a complete green flag 😢

Yes, Jude was a stalker at the beginning and kept repeating that he wanted to kill her, but if he truly wanted that, he would’ve done it right away. He couldn’t, because he knew her before the incident — she had helped him, and she’s known for helping everyone around her. Deep down, he knew that if she could, she would’ve helped again.

Sure, Jude is violent, impulsive, loves breaking things and punching people… but he’s incredibly gentle with his girl. He never forced her to do anything, and he even tried to put distance between them (because he learned something 👀). So when Dahlia asked violet, “What do you even see in this brute?” I laughed so hard — because the real brute is Kane 😂. Never judge someone solely based on their outward actions 🙅🏻‍♀️

And ohhh, the twists! There were so many, and I wasn’t expecting them at all. They were super fun and refreshing, and I loved every one of them.

There is absolutely nothing more entertaining than Preston — a true clown 🤡. And he’s still stuck with his issue of mispronouncing every name starting with “D” except Dahlia’s… and now he’s doing it again with every “V” name except violet’s. But he eventually started calling her “Vee,” which was adorable.
Nothing made me laugh like his teasing of Dahlia by calling her “Dakota.” I also loved that he still doesn’t like her and keeps threatening her 🤣 — unlike with Violet. And Jude’s jealousy?? Everything. Absolutely everything 👀🔥

I’m so sad about what happened to Mario 🥹🥹. I can’t get over it, and I really hope he won’t be forgotten so we can know what happens to him.

One thing I wished for is this: just like Jude changed violet, I wanted her to change him more too. Every time she told him to stop, he actually stopped. He did show some change, yes — but I wanted it to be bigger. I know he was raised to be a killer, but I hoped she’d push him to limit that side of him even more, only resorting to it when absolutely forced.

Overall: an emotional, wild, twisty, unexpectedly fun read — with a chaotic, intense couple I genuinely rooted for 💚🔥

"You can heal others, and I’ll protect you, sweetheart."

I honestly can’t choose whether I like Kane or Jude better. I loved them both in their books.

For me, Jude actually wasn’t that bad. At least he felt pretty tame compared to other MMCs Rina has written. I mean, yes, he still stalks Violet and hunts and murders people, but even though he said he wants to kill Violet at first, he never does anything truly hurtful to her (dark romance standards). He falls hard and fast, and the way he treats her is sooo sweet. I loved how proud he was whenever she stood up for herself. Especially in that one scene when she said she wore the dress for herself.
—> Also, he calls her sweetheart.🥹

Violet might not be as memorable an FMC as some others, but I really loved her. Her relationship with Dahlia and later also Preston was so wholesome. I didn’t even care that much about the spicy scenes, because I just enjoyed Jude and Violet’s interactions and all the friend group moments with Kane, Dahlia and Preston.

And the ending! Oh my god. I was so scared, and what happened to Preston completely shocked me! I knew his book was next, so somehow he couldn’t stay dead, but the way it happened made me question everything for a while. I was so glad for that epilogue. And Marcus! He completely lost it when he heard about Preston’s death.
In general, I love how protective they all are over Preston, especially Jude.

"Number 16 hit Preston, so I had to break his legs. I didn’t manage to actually do that and just flattened him against the ice, and so I found my way back to the annoying box."

One of my favorite scenes was the reading of the testament at the end. Preston’s will was honestly hilarious, and the way everything was revealed made me scream!

And once again, Rina Kent made me fall in love not only with Jude, but also with a bunch of side characters. I need a book about Julian & Annalise! And also about Atlas, Preston’s uncle. He only appeared briefly and there’s almost no information about him, but I’m intrigued.

I can’t even describe how excited I am for Tempting Venom. Preston was my favorite in this book and Marcus is so obsessed with him. I know I will love their book. June seems so far away.😭

I love some sweet unhinged heroes who are like cute teddy bears with their girls only 😌 This book is seriously a very modified and better version of her other books. I’m loving how Rina is making her new books better by incorporating readers’ feedback and not adding virgins in her books or making every guy a manwhore. The last thing she needs to stop doing is giving them dead eyes and we’ll be good!

If y’all loved Jeremy/Cecily, then this book is for you. The stalking trope is well done here and exactly similar to how it was done in God of Wrath. Either Jude stalks, or he sends his minion to stalk — either way, he’s getting ALL the reports.

At first I was wondering why he didn’t kill her like he did the other ones:
a) she’s pretty
b) main character duh

But turns out she showed him kindness once (the umbrella scene artwork), and he’s obviously attracted to how someone SO KIND just stood there watching her mother die. I actually devour these types of storylines. It was typical Rina Kent fashion but damn, I loved both characters, and Jude at least had a little bit of respect. I didn’t see him using weird words like “cumbag,” “trash,” or calling girls “holes,” so I think this bare minimum is a WIN WIN?

If you’ve read Book 1, you know Violet was in a coma for 3 months. This book actually showed scenes from before she was in the coma/how it happened, and after-it scenes that start from the end of Book 1. I loved how Jude was getting mad. Ngl, all the claiming/jealousy scenes were sooo good and it felt like I was reading God of Wrath again 😭 with new characters and new backstories.

“Because she chose death to fucking escape me.”

Julian lied to her, claiming that Jude tried to kill him so she became his lab rat for drug studies — weird fr. And with the whole plot twist revolving around it? More weird.

“So, yes, I’m back, even though I truly intended to let her go. Just kidding. I would’ve always only done that temporarily, but still, I was going to avoid contact with her for at least a month. Just kidding again. Because I was around. I couldn’t have avoided her when I’ve been roaming in her environment.”

Love myself an indecisive hero. Jude Callahan is a cutie <333


PRESTON: “It’s called kissing? Something you do a lot of with Daphne, remember?”
KANE: “You stay out of it.”
PRESTON: “No can do. I’m Jude’s defender for life, and I like Vee.”

I seriously loved Preston and Jude’s bond. I shipped them so hard while reading Book 1, but nvm, they’re besties!! And Preston actually liking Violet and being a genuine friend to her was so cute and affectionate. I just died with him being absolutely rude with Dahlia wjsjaj and calling her Dorothy, Dina, Diana — never her real name 😂😂 and ngl, I didn't care much about Dahlia and Kane in this book. The highlights were Preston/Marcus and Julian. Dahlia was literally just there jsjsjs

no hate tho, xoxo


“Come on, don’t make that face. You look so handsome when you smile instead. Besides, this is so much fun.”
Violet’s hand lands on my chest, and I can’t resist the hum that ripples through me. Jesus fuck. Her softness has always been my undoing. She touches me so gently that I’m ready to murder my entire bloodline for her. This ailment needs to be studied.”

AWWWHHHH THIS SCENE WAS SO CUTEEEE!!!! 💕🥺

“Sorry for the trauma dumping.” She smiles awkwardly. “I swear I don’t do this all the time. I guess… I really love talking to you about everything because you’ve always given me a safe space.”
“And I always will. Don’t be sorry for finally using your voice, Violet. I’m here for you.”

Jude and Violet healed each other and were absolute lovebirds. Even though there was a lot of angst and A LOT of push/pull — and that too from Jude’s side because of his mental issues — I loved how calm and understanding Violet was and how self-aware Jude was that he was hurting her.

“As long as you don’t hurt me anymore, I can forgive and forget. But don’t ice me out again.”
“I won’t. I’m sorry, sweetheart. I was having a hard time and didn’t want to burden you with it or take it out on you.”
“That’s the point of having each other, Jude.”
“Okay.”

Seriously, I was thinking about groveling, but Jude never did anything wrong. Well, the ghosting/stalking were weird, but I’m so happy this was a very sweet and raw book rather than pushing dubcon or roleplay on us. I love how emotional and beautiful both Violet and Jude were.
UM I ALSO READ IN A REVIEW THAT IT HAS DUBCON SCENES BUT NOPE?


“I can’t lose you,” he repeats softly, as soft as Jude can speak. “Don’t make me lose you, too, sweetheart. Even if it’s just out of pity, stay with me. Don’t push me away.”

OBSESSED AND DESPERATE JUDE. THE MAN WHO YEARNS IS A MAN WHO EARNS ‼️‼️

in my honest opinion, they both are just so good, the spice level of this book is OKAYISH, not heavy like her other books. I just lovvveeeeed their dynamic and how they both loved one another. I wanted yk more cute scenes though, but it was a little plot heavy.

- About his mother: well, what really happened was that his mother was abusive as well/toxic if I must say, but those were during her episodes and she was mentally unwell. Despite it all, she loved Jude and attempted suicide many times, but she didn’t want to hurt Jude or make him think his mother didn’t love him enough to live for him. She staged her own murder, though it resulted badly and she was stabbed 20 times. It’s seriously so fucked up.

I was a little confused about Jude’s father since he did seem a little caring toward him, but tbh I agree with Jude — no matter how much he’s “okay” now, he did use Jude and made him kill people in his childhood.

And about Lawrence (Preston’s father), their dynamic was giving Aiden/Jonathan vibes. Even while being emotionally unavailable, he did seem to care about his son — especially when he shouted that his ONLY son died. We need some bonding there ‼️

“The audacity to throw a party and not invite my highness.”

UGH [SPOILERS] — tbh Preston’s death scene (fake) and what happens afterward were so sad. Nobody should go through the grief of their best friend’s death and in Marcus’ case, “lover’s.” I genuinely felt so bad for everyone, and even though as a reader I knew he wasn’t dead because duh, it was still sad in the other characters’ POVs. His entry scene was hahahajaj very Landon King-coded and I loved it.

But most importantly, I’m so waiting for Marcus’ POV on all of this — he was obviously torn. There must be a reason, and ngl Preston’s mental health is no joke. I need proper cute scenes of them thank you sm.

Lastly, wdym rina?!!! NO JULIAN ANNALISE CRUMBS 😩

⌞RATINGS⌝

• Beautiful Venom (Dahlia & Kane) – 3.5 stars
• Tempting Venom (Marcus & Preston) – tbr

3.75⭐️
Yup, this was definitely better than Beautiful Venom. It was more enjoyable to read and significantly less cringey.
While it does feel very much like a copy and paste of Jeremy and Cecily’s story and honestly I usually eat that up it started to bother me in the last 100 pages.
The story became waaaay too predictable, and I found myself a little bored toward the ending, flipping pages and waiting for that signature RK ending.
That’s the main reason this wasn’t a 4⭐️ read for me.
At the end I just wanted to know what happened to Preston.

Violet got on my nerves a few times, her decisions were often questionable and downright infuriating. But at the same time, she’s such a sweet, kind soul with not a bad bone in her body and I can’t help but have a soft spot for her.
Everything she’s endured throughout her life made me sympathize with her deeply. She’s a total mama bear to Dahlia and I loved her kindness towards Laura and her child. Those moments were so sweet.
Violet truly loves helping people and being there for them and that compassion erases a lot of her bad decisions for me, because they always come from thinking about others, even when it doesn’t make sense.
Her and Preston were absolutely adorable, and their conversations made me smile from ear to ear 🥹😍
I wanted deeper conversations between her and Dahlia and more effort from Dahlia towards Violet. After everything they’ve been through I just expected their bond to be stronger.

I really liked Jude as well. His backstory absolutely broke my heart. Finding out what really happened to his mom was devastating, and I kept hoping it wasn’t true. Throughout the book he feels constantly torn between his rage and his emotions.
I loved watching him slowly peel back his layers and allow himself to be vulnerable and loved. He’s ruthless and intense but he would do absolutely anything for Violet just to see her smile.

The romance itself was sweet. They had me blushing and giggling 🥰🤭 but more importantly they truly showed up for each other and supported one another, which I loved. And I liked how they met each other way before what happened to his mom.

Once again Preston carried this book for me.
Every time Jude talked about him and their bond, my heart broke a little more.
I’m beyond desperate for his book at this point it’s not even funny.
And Marcus on his little killing rampage….omg 🫦
I am so seated for their story 🫶🏻

I still don’t understand the purpose of the secret society. It feels so unimportant to me that I literally forgot it existed until Jude mentioned it again at the end.

I did enjoy the hockey aspect, even though it’s not crucial to the plot. Loved to hear Jude’s inner thoughts during the games, how he views the game and his protectiveness over Preston.
And him trying to avoid the penalty box just so Violet could watch him play a full game 🤭

I think I would’ve enjoyed this book more if I’d taken a break between the two books.
At this point I’m a willing captive and I’ll read anything this woman writes and enjoy it 🙈

RK’s unavoidable allegations: from copycat criticism to slanders against women. 🚨

good evening, night owls and literary seekers. i’m vee, and this is midnights with vee, the only news hour that reads you the headlines while the candle burns low and the hearts race fast.


BREAKING: sweet venom, romance or re‑hash?

tonight, we’re pulling back the velvet curtain on rina kent, the author whose latest dark romance, sweet venom, has caused murmurs amongst the bookish community.

the plot or the copy‑paste?
our sources say the novel feels eerily familiar, like it could have been lifted straight from the third installment of the legacy of gods series, god of wrath.

jude, the tattooed covered bike rider who is on a killing spree of anyone who was a witness to his mother's murder, is essentially a temu version of jeremy from god of wrath.

- a failed stalker
- a stupid dumbfuck
- has mommy issues

violet, our doormat heroine who avoids violence like a nun avoids chocolate, mirrors cecily with all the nuance of a recycled love letter.

her inner monologues consisted of the following:
- my spine is tingling
- my heart is beating faster
- and vee loses her brain cell everytime


allegation #2: the women slander clause

readers have also lodged a formal complaint against the recurring trope of women as either:

• a doormat female main character
• a mentally unstable mother
• a female villain

the book seems to have taken a dark romance and turned it into a dark misogyny romance, leaving many fans wondering whether the author hates women or simply ran out of imagination.

audio only redemption
despite the whole drama, the audiobook version deserves a nod. narrator teddy hamlinton delivers the lines with such silky tone that even the most tired of us found a sliver of enjoyment.


what’s next?

tempting venom—the next instalment from the vipers series—arrives in 2026. will rina kent finally break the cycle? or give us god of fury or kiss the villain 2.0? stay tuned.


so, dear night readers, if you’re craving a romance that feels something dark and new, maybe wait for the next release. until then, keep your candles lit, your bookmarks ready, and remember: when the plot’s as plain as a soggy toast, the narrator’s voice is the only thing that can keep you from falling asleep.

a huge thank you to manas for reading this with me. i love you!!

this has been vee on midnights with vee. stay dark, stay dramatic.
